_source: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals (MDGL) Q2 2026 earnings call, 30 July 2026. Extraction output cached so the demo runs without an API key. Quotes are short verbatim spans; full transcript is not committed (see README, 'Data & licensing').

claims.claim: Madrigal's CEO cited proprietary market research claiming 80% of prescribers would not use lanifibranor because of weight gain.
claims.quote: 80% of prescribers said they wouldn't use lanifibranor because of the weight gain
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: A direct, quantified attack on IVA's only asset weeks before its Phase 3 topline. Whether or not the research is representative, it is the incumbent's stated launch playbook against IVA and sets the commercial bar lanifibranor must clear even on positive data.

claims.claim: Madrigal characterised lanifibranor's profile as a high-dose pill carrying weight gain and edema, framed against a market focused on weight loss.
claims.quote: It's a PPAR associated with weight gain and edema
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: Establishes the differentiation argument IVA will have to answer at launch. Inventiva's own disclosure puts weight gain near 30% of patients at 5% or more, so the attack has a factual anchor rather than being pure spin.

claims.claim: Madrigal's CMO suggested rival MASH sponsors are accruing trial events more slowly than Madrigal's F4c outcomes study.
claims.quote: in other programs at other sponsor companies are maybe not seeing as robust accrual of events
claims.speaker: David Allegretti
claims.reasoning: An unsolicited read on competitors' trial operations that names no one. Enrollment and event-accrual health is normally invisible from outside; a rival CMO volunteering it is a rare read-through on timelines across the whole indication.

claims.claim: Madrigal has not confirmed the target event count for the F4c outcomes trial, declining to endorse the number in the published trial design.
claims.quote: we haven't actually confirmed the target number of events
claims.speaker: David Allegretti
claims.reasoning: The event count sets trial duration. Refusing to confirm it while repeating a 2027 guide widens the readout window in both directions and is the single largest swing factor on the F4c opportunity.

claims.claim: Management repeated a 2027 F4c readout guide but declined to narrow it, deferring precision to a future update across four separate analyst questions.
claims.quote: Right now we're tracking to 2027, as we've said
claims.speaker: David Allegretti
claims.reasoning: The date is unchanged but the language around it is softer than prior quarters and four analysts pushed on it unsuccessfully. Sustained refusal to narrow an event-driven guide is the usual precursor to a slip.

claims.claim: Madrigal volunteered a critique of semaglutide's real-world MASH performance without being asked about it.
claims.quote: you have to stay on a drug, get to a high enough dose, and be on it long enough
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: Unprompted competitive commentary is disproportionately informative — the analyst did not raise semaglutide. Volunteering a persistence-based rebuttal suggests GLP-1 encroachment is being felt in the field even though reported numbers show no impact.

claims.claim: Madrigal booked a $25M upfront to in-license MGL-0795, a PNPLA3-targeting siRNA, from Arrowhead.
claims.quote: a one-time upfront business development expense of $25 million related to the in-licensing of MGL0795
claims.speaker: Mardi Dier
claims.reasoning: Confirms the shift from single-asset to combination strategy and puts a price on genotype-targeted MASH assets. Relevant to any holding with a PNPLA3 or siRNA position, and it re-rates what Arrowhead's platform is worth.

claims.claim: The US addressable F2/F3 MASH population grew from 315,000 to 460,000 diagnosed patients over two years.
claims.quote: the U.S. addressable market has grown nearly 50%, from 315,000 diagnosed F2/F3 patients
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: Expands the denominator for every F2/F3 entrant, not just Madrigal. Inventiva guides to roughly 375,000 addressable patients — a live discrepancy in the market-size assumption underpinning both names.

claims.claim: Rezdiffra Q2 net sales were $364.3M, up 71% year over year, with over 49,000 active patients.
claims.quote: Second quarter 2026 net sales were $364 million, representing year-over-year growth of 71%
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: In line with the trajectory and consensus. Establishes the commercial baseline a competitor entrant would have to displace, but does not by itself shift the view.

claims.claim: Madrigal secured three additional patents this month, including one covering the unapproved F4c indication.
claims.quote: This month, we build on that foundation with three additional patents
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: Extends exclusivity into the 2040s and complicates skinny-label generic entry. Secondary to near-term competitive dynamics but raises the barrier for anyone entering the same mechanism class.

claims.claim: European contribution is negligible and expected to stay so this year, with reimbursement blocked by unresolved most-favoured-nation pricing policy.
claims.quote: contribution of Europe is negligible in the quarter, and we would expect that to be for the year
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: An industry-wide pricing overhang rather than a company-specific problem, but it removes ex-US upside from the near-term model and applies equally to any holding planning a European launch.

claims.claim: Prescribing remains concentrated among hepatologists and gastroenterologists, with endocrinology roughly nine months into its launch.
claims.quote: This continues to be driven by Hepatitis C and GIs, for the most part
claims.speaker: Bill Sibold
claims.reasoning: Routine channel colour. Included mainly because the source text is mis-transcribed and shows why literal keyword matching on transcripts is unreliable.
claims.transcription_note: Vendor ASR error: 'Hepatitis C' is a mis-transcription of 'hepatologists'. A keyword rule would have filed this under an infectious disease indication.
